scenario_text: An NBFC wants to build an AI-based credit risk scoring engine but they're not sure exactly what data sources to use or what the model architecture should look like. There's significant technical risk — they've never built ML systems before. Budget is uncertain and depends on initial results. They want to build a proof of concept first before committing to full development.

requirements.statement: The system shall support the integration of multiple data sources for credit risk scoring
requirements.business_justification: Using diverse data sources improves the accuracy and robustness of the credit risk model
requirements.assumptions: Data sources will be available in structured formats such as CSV, JSON, or API endpoints
requirements.acceptance_criteria: The system successfully connects to and retrieves data from at least three different data sources

requirements.statement: The system shall provide a modular and configurable model architecture for credit risk scoring
requirements.business_justification: A modular architecture allows for flexibility in model design and facilitates future enhancements
requirements.assumptions: The system will use a framework that supports modular development, such as Python with scikit-learn or TensorFlow
requirements.acceptance_criteria: The system allows for the addition, removal, or modification of model components without affecting the overall system functionality

requirements.statement: The system shall support the creation of a proof of concept (PoC) with limited data and functionality
requirements.business_justification: A PoC allows the organization to validate the feasibility of the system before full-scale development
requirements.assumptions: The PoC will use a subset of the data and a simplified version of the model architecture
requirements.acceptance_criteria: The PoC demonstrates basic credit risk scoring functionality using a limited dataset and simplified model

requirements.statement: The system shall provide a user interface for monitoring and evaluating model performance
requirements.business_justification: Monitoring model performance is essential for ensuring accuracy, fairness, and compliance with regulatory requirements
requirements.assumptions: The interface will display key performance metrics such as accuracy, precision, recall, and F1 score
requirements.acceptance_criteria: The system includes a dashboard that displays model performance metrics in real-time

requirements.statement: The system shall allow for the storage and retrieval of model versions for audit and compliance purposes
requirements.business_justification: Storing model versions ensures traceability and supports regulatory audits
requirements.assumptions: The system will use a version control system such as Git or a dedicated model registry
requirements.acceptance_criteria: The system maintains a record of all model versions with timestamps and metadata

requirements.statement: The system shall provide documentation and training materials for users and developers
requirements.business_justification: Documentation and training are essential for onboarding new users and ensuring proper system usage
requirements.assumptions: The documentation will cover system setup, model training, and deployment processes
requirements.acceptance_criteria: The system includes comprehensive documentation and training materials accessible to authorized users

requirements.statement: The system shall support the evaluation of model fairness and bias
requirements.business_justification: Ensuring model fairness is critical to avoid discrimination and comply with ethical and regulatory standards
requirements.assumptions: The system will use fairness metrics such as demographic parity, equal opportunity, and disparate impact
requirements.acceptance_criteria: The system includes tools to evaluate and report on model fairness across different demographic groups

requirements.statement: The system shall support the deployment of the model in a test environment before full production
requirements.business_justification: Deploying in a test environment allows for validation of system performance and stability before production use
requirements.assumptions: The test environment will mirror the production environment as closely as possible
requirements.acceptance_criteria: The system can be deployed and tested in a separate environment without affecting production operations

requirements.statement: The system shall provide a mechanism for handling missing or incomplete data in the credit risk model
requirements.business_justification: Handling missing data is essential for maintaining model accuracy and reliability
requirements.assumptions: The system will use imputation techniques or flag missing data for manual review
requirements.acceptance_criteria: The system includes functionality to detect, handle, and report on missing or incomplete data

requirements.statement: The system shall support the use of both supervised and unsupervised learning techniques for credit risk scoring
requirements.business_justification: Using a combination of learning techniques can improve model performance and adaptability
requirements.assumptions: The system will use a machine learning framework that supports both supervised and unsupervised learning
requirements.acceptance_criteria: The system allows for the implementation of both supervised and unsupervised learning models

requirements.statement: The system shall provide real-time monitoring of model performance metrics during the proof of concept phase.
requirements.acceptance_criteria: The system shall display accuracy, precision, recall, and F1-score metrics in real-time on the user interface.

requirements.statement: The system shall support the rollback of model versions in case of performance degradation or errors.
requirements.acceptance_criteria: The system shall allow administrators to revert to a previously stored model version within 5 minutes of detecting an issue.

requirements.statement: The system shall provide automated alerts for model performance degradation beyond predefined thresholds.
requirements.acceptance_criteria: The system shall send email and in-app notifications to administrators when model performance drops by 10% or more from the baseline.

requirements.statement: The system shall support the configuration of data source priorities and fallback mechanisms.
requirements.acceptance_criteria: The system shall allow administrators to define a priority order for data sources and automatically switch to a backup source if the primary one fails.

requirements.statement: The system shall provide a mechanism for tracking and logging all user interactions with the model during the proof of concept phase.
requirements.acceptance_criteria: The system shall store a log of all user actions, including model configuration changes and evaluation requests, for at least 30 days.

requirements.statement: The system shall support the generation of performance reports for model evaluation and stakeholder review.
requirements.acceptance_criteria: The system shall generate a downloadable PDF report containing model performance metrics, fairness analysis, and data source utilization every 24 hours.

requirements.statement: The system shall support the simulation of different credit scenarios to test model robustness.
requirements.acceptance_criteria: The system shall allow users to input custom credit scenarios and receive model predictions and confidence scores for each scenario.

requirements.statement: The system shall provide a user interface for managing and configuring model training parameters.
requirements.acceptance_criteria: The system shall allow users to adjust hyperparameters, training epochs, and batch sizes through a graphical interface.

requirements.statement: The system shall support the integration of external model evaluation tools for third-party validation.
requirements.acceptance_criteria: The system shall provide an API endpoint that allows external tools to connect and evaluate model performance.

requirements.statement: The system shall provide a mechanism for anonymizing personal data used in model training and evaluation.
requirements.acceptance_criteria: The system shall automatically replace personal identifiers with pseudonyms before model training begins.

issues.description: The term 'multiple data sources' is vague and not quantified. It should specify a minimum number of data sources.
issues.suggestion: Revise the statement to specify a measurable number, e.g., 'The system shall support the integration of at least three data sources for credit risk scoring.'

issues.description: The term 'modular and configurable model architecture' is vague and not quantified. It should define what modularity and configurability mean in this context.
issues.suggestion: Revise the statement to include measurable criteria, e.g., 'The system shall allow for the addition, removal, or modification of at least five model components without affecting the overall system functionality.'

issues.description: The term 'limited data and functionality' is vague and not quantified. It should define what 'limited' means in this context.
issues.suggestion: Revise the statement to include measurable criteria, e.g., 'The system shall support the creation of a proof of concept (PoC) using a dataset containing no more than 10,000 records and a simplified model with no more than three features.'

criteria.reasoning: The requirements are not well known or easily defined as the NBFC is still working out what data sources to use and what the model architecture should look like.
The requirements cannot be defined early in the cycle as the NBFC is uncertain about data sources and model architecture.
The requirements are likely to change often in the cycle as the NBFC is not sure exactly what data sources to use or what the model architecture should look like.
There is a need to demonstrate the requirements to achieve definition as the NBFC wants to build a proof of concept first before committing to full development.
A proof of concept is required to demonstrate capability as the NBFC has significant technical risk and has never built ML systems before.
The project is focused on building a proof of concept for an existing business function (credit risk scoring), not a new product direction.
The requirement to integrate multiple data sources implies interoperability with external systems, which is a hallmark of a system integration project.
The project is not an enhancement to an existing system but rather the creation of a new system from scratch, starting with a proof of concept.

The project is focused on a proof of concept with uncertain future, not a long-lived infrastructure system.

The statement does not mention the team's experience with the problem domain (business area).

advantages.advantage: Risk assessed and addressed every cycle
advantages.relevance: REQ-007 requires evaluating model fairness and bias, which demands continuous risk assessment and mitigation throughout the project lifecycle.

advantages.advantage: Expensive commitments deferred until risk drops
advantages.relevance: REQ-001 and REQ-003 indicate that data sources and model architecture are not well defined, so deferring costly decisions until later stages aligns with the project's uncertainty.
REQ-003 mandates the creation of a proof of concept, which Spiral supports by integrating prototyping with planning to ensure alignment with evolving requirements.

advantages.advantage: Natural stopping points if funding changes
advantages.relevance: REQ-004 and REQ-008 require deployment in a test environment and monitoring of model performance, which can be paused or adjusted based on funding availability.

justifications.gives_up: Spiral assumes this takes the organisation somewhere it has not been before, and that the product will be running for years — neither is true here, so that part of its design earns nothing on this project.

sdlc.cross_check_reasoning: Agile is the most suitable SDLC model as it supports iterative development, which aligns with the high-priority requirements for creating a proof of concept, integrating multiple data sources, and ensuring model fairness and compliance. It also allows for continuous feedback and adaptation, which is essential for handling complex and evolving requirements in a credit risk scoring system.

questions.question: About “The system shall provide a mechanism for anonymizing personal data used in model training and evaluation”: The requirement does not specify a stakeholder or source for the requirement. The field 'stakeholder' is set to 'Not specified'. (For example: Identify the stakeholder or source that originated this requirement and update the 'stakeholder' field accordingly.)

About “The system shall provide a mechanism for handling missing or incomplete data in the credit risk model”: The term 'credit risk model' is used without a definition. A reader cannot look it up in a published source unless it is explicitly defined in the requirement. (For example: Define 'credit risk model' in the requirement or reference an external document where it is defined.)

About “The system shall provide a modular and configurable model architecture for credit risk scoring”: The term 'modular and configurable model architecture' is vague and not quantified. It should define what modularity and configurability mean in this context. (For example: Revise the statement to include measurable criteria, e.g., 'The system shall allow for the addition, removal, or modification of at least five model components without affecting the overall system functionality.'.)

About “The system shall provide a user interface for managing and configuring model training parameters”: The requirement does not specify a stakeholder or source for the requirement. The field 'stakeholder' is set to 'Not specified'. (For example: Identify the stakeholder or source that originated this requirement and update the 'stakeholder' field accordingly.)

About “The system shall provide documentation and training materials for users and developers”: The term 'comprehensive documentation and training materials' is vague and not quantified. It should define what 'comprehensive' means in this context. (For example: Revise the statement to include measurable criteria, e.g., 'The system shall provide documentation and training materials covering at least 10 key topics related to system setup, model training, and deployment processes.'.)

About “The system shall support the creation of a proof of concept (PoC) with limited data and functionality”: The term 'limited data and functionality' is vague and not quantified. It should define what 'limited' means in this context. (For example: Revise the statement to include measurable criteria, e.g., 'The system shall support the creation of a proof of concept (PoC) using a dataset containing no more than 10,000 records and a simplified model with no more than three features.'.)
